runs.failure_point: A timed-out store-wide scan silently skipped a block of matters; all later listing, scanning and reading worked from the partial hit set, so one qualifying deal never surfaced and the answer named two of three.

first_error.stage: Scan document text with an extraction script
first_error.critic_note: (specific flag) The scan-stage review at [33] said the timed-out range rerun was never checked for completion of every range; the agent did not check and built every later step from the 141 matters in the partial output.
first_error.why: The background range scans were cut by the 60 s timeout before reaching a block of matters that held one qualifying deal, and the agent never checked range coverage or read its saved financing path list, so that matter never entered the candidate set.

divergence: Mixed (T0, T2 pass; T1 fails). All three runs listed the whole store, ran a store-wide extraction scan that timed out, and got a review flagging unverified coverage. They split at that scan stage: T0 reran the scan in twelve small chunks writing one line per matter, and T2 checked each range file's scanned-matter count against the 266-matter inventory, so both reached the three qualifying deals; T1 combined the partial outputs of six timed-out background ranges without checking them and drew every later step (three agent-defined listing stages, a second scan of only the 141 hit matters, two reading stages) from that set, which lacked one qualifying matter. The reviews did not differ: T1's scan review named the unchecked range coverage, and the agent moved on. Label notes and policy played no role; T1's agent-defined stages narrowed work to the partial hit set rather than widening it.
